revisions.title: Name the user, threatened information and workflow; validate demand
revisions.change: Add one specific user group/country, the sensitive documents they handle, the adversary and current workaround. Obtain consent-safe interviews or a partner request. Treat intended civic users in the spec as a hypothesis until validated.
revisions.check: At least one inspectable demand artifact and a clear harm → workflow → intervention chain; publish no sensitive identities.
revisions.lesson: The selected precedents explicitly protect civic/source/communication workflows. This supports user-specific framing, not a claim their applications contained demand validation.

revisions.title: Turn module contracts into a costed delivery plan
revisions.change: Add accountable lead, team experience, calendar, dependencies and milestone acceptance criteria: minimum local prototype, independent review, partner pilot, stable release and maintenance handover. Choose actual duration and staffing instead of invented commitments.
revisions.check: Each milestone has owner, date, deliverable, verification and cost; claimed team availability is confirmed.
revisions.lesson: The dated deployment/product-maturity awards demonstrate bounded funded work. They do not reveal the original application schedule.

revisions.title: Explain the tool's distinct place beside secure-submission systems
revisions.change: Add a workflow diagram showing where sensitive text enters, what is transformed, where the key/map lives, who can restore it, and what optional QA sends off-device. Compare content pseudonymization with secure transport, document isolation and metadata removal. Do not claim those are interchangeable.
revisions.check: Each claimed improvement has a testable baseline comparison; restoration rights and residual context risks are explicit.
revisions.lesson: SecureDrop/GlobaLeaks protect document receipt/handling. Neither establishes a funded reversible-pseudonymization mechanism in this sample.

revisions.title: Replace broad safety claims with a privacy–utility–adoption evaluation plan
revisions.change: Add the KPI plan below with baseline, denominator, test corpus, target-setting process, independent reviewer and measurement date. Report per-language/entity failure rates rather than one aggregate accuracy number.
revisions.check: Targets are agreed after baseline measurement; privacy misses and utility failures are both reported with uncertainty.
revisions.lesson: Sponsored assessments and usability-focused deployment support motivate inspectable evaluation. Exact KPI thresholds are analyst recommendations, not inferred winning thresholds.

revisions.title: Budget independent security and restoration review
revisions.change: Include external review of key/map access, storage/log exposure, restoration correctness, surrogate collisions, QA export boundaries and adversarial context inference; document remediation and retest. Separate local-only deployment from optional cloud modes.
revisions.check: Reviewer scope, cost and deliverables are explicit; no independent validation claim until the report exists.
revisions.lesson: These are sponsored assessment precedents, a different instrument from a cash development award.

revisions.title: Secure a pilot and a maintenance/adoption owner
revisions.change: Add an eligible partner's confirmed pilot workflow, integration owner, onboarding/support responsibilities and a post-grant maintenance plan. Specify language/hardware constraints and safe training materials.
revisions.check: Pilot commitment and maintenance responsibility documented; field use has a consent and feedback plan.
revisions.lesson: Product maturity, easy deployment and usability recur in close technical comparators. Actual partner commitments remain a proposal requirement to obtain.
revisions.status: Unknown proposal evidence, not established defect

revisions.title: Supply a transparent activity-linked budget and ask
revisions.change: State requested amount, duration, rates, work allocation, audit/user-research costs, accessible deployment and maintenance. Show any co-financing only when the selected call requires it.
revisions.check: Every cost maps to a deliverable and an eligible cost category; totals reconcile with the funding request.
revisions.lesson: Public award amounts are not original budget evidence. This revision rests on official application criteria, so historical-neighbor support is deliberately zero.

revisions.title: Make open release concrete while protecting real data
revisions.change: Specify the deliverable code/license, release tags, install documentation, synthetic benchmarks and public remediation notes. Keep source documents, keys and restoration maps out of shared artifacts.
revisions.check: Public artifacts are usable without the sensitive corpus; an owner is assigned for releases and support.
revisions.lesson: These precedents explicitly expose reusable tools. Open distribution strengthens reuse; it does not make confidential beneficiary data publishable.
revisions.status: Conditional criterion: exact license rules vary by funder

revisions.title: Write the abstract around a bounded user outcome
revisions.change: Use a plain-language problem, mechanism, deliverable, beneficiary outcome and ask. Say pseudonymization where mapping exists. State local/cloud boundaries, expected failure modes and human review rather than absolute anonymity or quantified funding odds.
revisions.check: A reader can identify who benefits, how, what will be delivered and what remains risky in one paragraph.
revisions.lesson: The strongest analogues describe a specific protective workflow, not a generic claim about AI or privacy.
